answer: Each identity must bind one grid-registered mesa solar array: the grid atlas records title, meter and output, one array backs one identity, duplicates rejected, weight after 30 metered days. One fake costs one real array: 6,000 units plus a 400-unit connection fee and 30 days of generation; 100 fakes cost 640,000 units and 100 sites. The cheapest cheat is renting an array, but the owner surrenders the array backing their own identity, generation is metered to one key, and a silent panel earns nothing; each identity is one vertex of the ownership graph, so two sharing one array collapse.
